hook: Blue light, sensed by phototropin, sets the direction of a liverwort spore's first cell division
hook_turn: sets the direction of a liverwort spore's first cell division
summary: In Marchantia spores, the first asymmetric division, which sets the plant's first body axis, is oriented by blue light detected by the photoreceptor phototropin. The signal also needs the protein NCH1. This is one liverwort species under lab conditions, so how widely plants use this cue is unknown.
title: Phototropin-mediated blue light signaling orients the asymmetry of Marchantia polymorpha spores.
